name: sentry
description: Build/Runs your crystal application, watches files, and rebuilds/restarts app on file changes

documents.title: Introducción
documents.text: Sentry 🤖 Build/Runs your crystal application, watches files, and rebuilds/reruns app on file changes

If it does not work, simply: (1) place the files located in the src dir into a your project in a dev/ dir, and (2) compile sentry by doing crystal build --release dev/sentry cli.cr -o ./sentry .

documents.title: Override Default Build Command
documents.text: The default build command is crystal build ./src/[app name].cr . The release flag is omitted by default for faster compilation time while you are developing.

documents.title: Override Default Files to Watch
documents.text: The default files being watched are ["./src/ / .cr", "./src/ / .ecr"] . By specifying files to watch, the default will be omitted. So if you want to watch all of the file in your src directory, you will need to specify that like in the above example.

documents.title: Setting Build or Run Arguments
documents.text: If you prefer granularity, you can specify arguments to the build or run commands using the --build-args or --run-args flags followed by a string of arguments.

documents.title: Running shards install Before Starting
documents.text: This is especially usefull when initiating Sentry from a Dockerfile or package.json file. It guarantees all the shards are installed before running.

documents.title: Reading Configurations from a File
documents.text: Sentry will automatically read configurations from .sentry.yml if it exists. This can be changed with -c FILE or --config=FILE . See the YAML.mapping definition in the Config class in the /src/sentry.cr file for valid file properties.

documents.title: Removing Colorization
documents.text: Sentry output is colorized by default. To remove colorization, pass the --no-color argument. Example

documents.title: Why?
documents.text: (1) It is tiring to have to stop and restart an app on every change. (2) Docker! Stop and restarting your app is especially expensive (and annoying) when running the app in a docker container, where one would need to totally rebuild the docker image for every change. Now, for development, simply run sentry in your docker container, and it will rebuild the app from the docker container on any changes, without rebuilding the docker image/container.

documents.title: Disclaimer
documents.text: Sentry is intended for use in a development environment, where failure is safe and expected 😉.
